summary.title: Front-end Developer Handbook 2019
summary.one_liner: A yearly curated guide to the state of front-end development in 2019, covering what the discipline is, how to learn it, the core web technologies, and the tooling in use.
keywords: how to become a front-end developer
takeaways: Front-end development means building HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the web platform, which may also run in headless browsers, webviews, or native runtimes.
Learn the underlying technologies (HTML, CSS, DOM, JavaScript) before abstractions like jQuery, Sass, JSX, or TypeScript.
Front-end job titles (e.g. front-end engineer, UI developer, accessibility expert) signal different skill sets, and the handbook explains each.
The 2019 edition summarizes trends such as React releases, CSS Grid and Flexbox support, ES modules, Cypress for end-to-end testing, Parcel vs Webpack, Babel 7, and GraphQL adoption.
summary.summary: This is the 2019 edition of an annual handbook from Frontend Masters, written as a curated guide for practising and aspiring front-end developers and for managers or recruiters. It opens with a recap of the year's trends and predictions, then explains the discipline, the runtimes front-end code targets (browsers, headless browsers, webviews, native), and a suggested learning order. It also covers job-title meanings and gives short definitions with specification links for core technologies such as HTML, CSS, HTTP, URLs, the DOM, JavaScript, and JSON. The visible text ends before the later chapters on tools and information outlets.
